leap.definition:
n. a light, self-propelled movement upwards or forwards
n. an abrupt transition
n. the distance leaped (or to be leaped)
v. pass abruptly from one state or topic to another
leap.translation:
n. 跳跃, 剧增, 急变, 被越过之物
vi. 跳跃, 突然经过
vt. 跃过, 使跃过

leap at.translation: 急于接受,欣然接受,抢着…

leap-frogged.translation: (leap-frog 的过去分词) 跳背戏

leaped.definition:
v move forward by leaps and bounds
v pass abruptly from one state or topic to another
v jump down from an elevated point
v cause to jump or leap

leaper.definition: n someone who bounds or leaps (as in competition)

leapers.definition:
plural of leaper
n someone who bounds or leaps (as in competition)
leapers.translation: (leaper 的复数) n. 跳跃者

leapfrog.definition:
n. advancing as if in the child's game, by leaping over obstacles or competitors
n. a game in which one child bends down and another leaps over
v. jump across
leapfrog.translation:
n. 跳背游戏, 竞相提高
vi. 跳背, 交替前进
vt. 跃过

leapfrog position.translation: [医] 跳娃位, 跳背戏位

leapfrogged.definition:
v. jump across
v. progress by large jumps instead of small increments
leapfrogged.translation: v. 跳背, 交替前进, 跃过( leapfrog的过去式和过去分词 )

leapfrogging.definition:
v jump across
v progress by large jumps instead of small increments

leapfrogs.definition:
n advancing as if in the child's game, by leaping over obstacles or competitors
n a game in which one child bends down and another leaps over
v jump across
v progress by large jumps instead of small increments
leapfrogs.translation: v. 跳背, 交替前进, 跃过( leapfrog的第三人称单数 )

leaping.translation: a. 跳跃的, 跳跃而行的

leapingly.translation: adv. 跳跃地, 用于跳跃地
